overview: This one-page file index concerns wages and hours of labor in the Japanese merchant marine. It lists four records—principally communications associated with the U.S. consulate at Kobe and a request from the Department of Commerce—covering average wages by crew rating, instructions to obtain wage information, reported changes since a July 29, 1933 consular report, and a cross-reference to file 800.866/92. The underlying telegrams, report, and departmental communication are described but are not reproduced in the supplied OCR.

subfiles.title: List of papers on wages and hours of Japanese seamen
subfiles.about: An index identifies four records concerning wages paid to crews of Japanese merchant vessels and related requests for information.
subfiles.summary: The sheet records a Kobe report giving average Japanese merchant-marine wages by crew rating and an instruction to telegraph the information. It also notes a Kobe telegram from Donovan stating that complete data had appeared in the consulate’s report of July 29, 1933, with only subsequent changes being supplied. A Department of Commerce communication confirms a telephone request to obtain the information from a consular officer in Japan, while a further Kobe report is cross-referenced to file 800.866/92.

interest: The sheet is useful as a documentary roadmap even though the indexed communications themselves are absent from the supplied text. It points historians to a detailed wage survey organized by occupational rank and establishes a chain of information-gathering between the Department of Commerce, the State Department, and the Kobe consulate. Its reference to a July 29, 1933 report and to file 800.866/92 may help locate fuller statistical evidence elsewhere in the archival series.
